_about: Say nothing twice. Krish, 2026-10-17: "Asa, everything I say to you, whether it's feedback or ideas, you should always be thinking about why I'm saying it and what that means for the future. I want a \"say nothing twice\" policy in this engine, where you understand me, how we work, and how we iterate." Every piece of feedback or idea he gives becomes one entry: his exact words (an excerpt, never a transcript), why he said it, what it means from now on, and where it is now enforced, each place with a marker that must stay there. scripts/check_failures.py (run first in every session) fails when a marker is gone, and lists the learnings still open. A failure he raised goes in config/failures.json; everything else he says goes here.

learnings.krish: the fact that I need to approve/sign off on titles and headers and thumbnail headings and whatnot after recording is an important distinction because only after recording do I really feel like I've got a message. Usually I change or understand a fair bit more after reading a script out loud than I do creating a script.
learnings.why: Reading the script aloud is where he finds his message, and he ad-libs a third of it (narration ledger). Packaging written before the take is written for a message he has not landed yet, so it gets redone.
learnings.means: No title, headline, thumbnail word, card heading or chapter divider is put to him or drawn before a take is on the record; after it, the options come from what he said on camera and his playbook, all at once.

learnings.krish: This isn't a well-known concept and it's not a well-known media business. ... Why can't you understand why I absolutely hate, detest, loathe these? They're offensive to me. They hurt my soul.
learnings.why: His purpose is to make what is coming legible to people; a line only legible to someone who has already watched the video is the opposite of it, and a cheap, cryptic one costs the credibility a new brand for senior people depends on. It also proved lessons already on file were ignored: the surface formula ("under 4 words", "a curiosity gap") was followed over his principle.
learnings.means: Every line a stranger sees first names a real thing in plain words and says something true about it; his principles outrank any formula; nothing reaches him before a cold reader with no context can explain it; fewer, better options, never a pile.

learnings.why: He wants the engine cheaper to run (half a 20x Max plan in one week, $45.51 of API in seven days), but a saving that makes the work worse is not a saving to him.

A cost change is measured first: one that the meter shows saves nothing is not made.
